spec.summary: Add an adaptive-attack lane that searches new evasion axes (field obfuscation, timing, noise and state exhaustion) and turns the results into a per-rule evasion-cost vector with a ratcheted published floor. Each finding is classified as inherent to threshold rules (reported, never "fixed") or as a bug. A fast probe session (about 0.1 s per probe instead of 3.5-4.7 s) makes it affordable. Probing the uncommitted tree already turned up three bugs the current harness cannot see: a cross-window sweep in DequeWindowCounter, no identity canonicalisation in WS-4 group keys, and attribution forgery through the SSH username. All are described under approach.
files_to_modify: run_all_tests.sh (add three stanzas after the existing evasion_search stanza at ~line 504: test_evasion_axes.py, evasion_cost.py --seed 7, noise_dilution.py --blocking-subset; the file is dirty in the working tree, so rebase carefully)

eval/adversarial/evasion_search.py (one optional, parity-gated change: make _fired() delegate to probe_session when available, with env FENGARDE_SLOW_PROBE=1 as the escape hatch; all other behaviour byte-identical)
eval/adversarial/README.md (document the new axes, the cost vector and the floor ratchet)
contracts/detection-coverage.md (append a generated 'Evasion cost' table; the file is dirty in the working tree)
SSOT.md (new rows with PROVEN/ASSUMED marking; the file is dirty in the working tree)
.github/workflows/ci.yml (only if the owner approves a nightly full lane; the blocking lane needs no change because CI calls run_all_tests.sh)
spec.approach:
VERIFIED STARTING POINT (read and probed on the uncommitted tree, seed 7, read-only).
(1) Today's evasion_search covers four axes (loss, pacing/stretch, ip_k, account_k) for 6 burst steps. Its _detects() calls report._real_detection -> negative_controls.run_pipeline, which builds a fresh Detector(plugin_rule_dirs=[]) on every probe. Detector construction costs about 2.4 s of the 3.5-4.7 s per probe; normalising and processing 12 events takes 0.07 s. A full existing search took 328 s (it_intrusion 227.7 s, infra_takeover 99.4 s) while the test gate was also running.
(2) 18 shipped rules are stateful and only 10 are exercised by a storyline. The 8 with no evasion measurement at all are agent_tool_call_burst, bank_mass_card_read, common_beaconing (periodicity max_cv 0.25), common_bruteforce_sourceless, common_impossible_travel, common_password_spray, common_rapid_account_lifecycle and ot_new_engineering_connection.
(3) evasion_search._rule_params ignores siem.periodicity and companion_of, and its hard-coded {src_endpoint.ip: ip_k, actor.user.name: account_k} map cannot express other group keys.

FINDINGS THE NEW AXES MUST REPRODUCE (these justify the design and become the first controls).
F1 BUG, cross-window sweep. services/shared/window.py DequeWindowCounter._sweep() evicts every idle key using the CURRENT hit's window_ms (every _SWEEP_EVERY=256 hits). Direct repro: hit_distinct('long', t0, 300000, 'h1'); then 255 hit() calls on other keys with a 60000 ms window at t0+100 s; then hit_distinct('long', t0+100 s, 300000, 'h2') returns 1 instead of 2 (the no-noise control returns 2). Noise on any short-window rule therefore wipes live state of longer-window rules: lateral_movement (300 s), password_spray (300 s), bank_mass_card_read (300 s), ot_new_engineering_connection (600 s), and the 3600 s rules common_beaconing, common_impossible_travel and common_rapid_account_lifecycle. The Redis backend uses per-key EXPIRE, so the two backends disagree. Existing tests only cover same-window sweeps. Only the primitive is proven; the end-to-end proof is this step's job.
F2 BUG, identity canonicalisation. WS-4 groups on the raw str(actor.user.name) (engine.py _evaluate_stateful, group = str(group_value)). WS-8 canonicalises actors with strip().casefold() (shared.entity_helpers.canonical_entity_value via canonical_entity_id), and dns_query.parent_domain lower-cases and strips the trailing dot. Measured end to end on it_intrusion lateral_movement: 2 source addresses alone are detected, but 2 addresses plus one account respelled (upper-case, 'CORP\deploy', or trailing space) are NOT detected (both common_lateral_movement and its by_source companion go dark). Windows accounts are case-insensitive, so this evasion is free. The same probe on dns_exfil (case, trailing dot, deeper subdomain) was still detected, which is the robust-control case. On linux_ssh, case variants also evade the ip2 pair, but POSIX usernames are case-sensitive, so that one is INHERENT (it reduces to wasted guesses).
F3 BUG, attribution forgery. linux_ssh parsing of 'Failed password for invalid user x from 198.18.9.9 port 1 ssh2 Failed password for y from 203.0.113.21 ...' yields src_endpoint.ip=198.18.9.9 and user=x. The attacker-chosen username moves the group key of a different field. Measured at parser level. The single-account variant stayed detected end to end because the by-account rule still sees one account, so full evasion needs a joint (ip x account) move.
F4 TRUST-MODEL. windows_eventlog, vmware_vsphere and cloudtrail take event time from the record's own timestamp and ignore meta.received_at; linux_ssh does the reverse. mutate_generic.set_time moves both, so today's timing axes cannot see this. Forging the record clock stretches a burst for free where the source is attacker-influenced. This is inherent to the trust model, to be reported with its owner decision.
F5 INVARIANT. Scorer.score is a pure function of the matched rules, so alert volume cannot dilute a score. Alert ids are rule:group:window-bucket (Rule.alert_key), so 100-450 flood events on one rule and group collapsed to at most 2 alert ids in my probe; event floods do not create alert floods. WS-8 member_cap (DEFAULT_MEMBER_CAP=200) evicts the oldest members of a same-entity track, so only about 200 or more DISTINCT same-entity alerts can truncate an attack's membership. Disjoint-entity noise measured contamination 0.0.

DESIGN.
5a probe_session.py (speed, prerequisite for everything else). FastProbe builds ONE Detector(plugin_rule_dirs=[], rules_dir=optional) and per call: normalises through negative_controls._get_ws2().normalize_one with a cache keyed on sha256 of (source_type, raw, meta); swaps in a fresh shared.window.DequeWindowCounter (detector._window_counter = c; r.set_counter(c) for every stateful rule, mirroring Detector._load); stamps siem.tenant, ingest_id and twin_step exactly as negative_controls.run_pipeline does; and returns the same dict shape. verify_parity(sdef, seed) asserts identical fired lists against report._real_detection on the baseline and on 3 perturbed streams. The rules_dir parameter lets controls run against a mutated COPY of contracts/rules in a temp directory without touching the repo. Expected cost is about 0.1 s per probe, which makes 2-D and 3-D grids and multi-seed runs affordable.
5b Axis 1, field obfuscation (evasion_axes.py plus evasion_tables.yaml). Reuse mutate_generic.get_/set_ adapters and extend them with a verify-by-parse step: every operator re-normalises and reports the OCSF path it actually changed.
  - evasion_tables.yaml ATTACKER_CONTROL maps (source_type, raw_field) to {ocsf_path, attacker_controlled: yes|no|conditional, basis}. Examples: ssh username yes; DNS QNAME yes; sshd 'Failed password' text no (server-generated; the lower-case variant is dead-lettered but not attacker-reachable); Windows TargetUserName conditional; TCP source address no. Operators only run on attacker-controlled fields; everything else is listed as not_searched with its reason, never silently skipped.
  - IDENTITY_EQUIV per field kind with a cited basis: windows_account (casefold, strip, DOMAIN\ prefix, @upn), dns_name (casefold, trailing dot, IDNA), posix_user (identity), cloud_arn (identity), ip (ipaddress canonical form).
  - Operators with the mutate_generic contract (payloads, ctx) -> (payloads, changed): case_alt, pad (space, NBSP, ZWSP), domain_prefix, upn_suffix, unicode forms (NFC/NFD/fullwidth/homoglyph), percent/base64/hex encodings for web_access and n8n fields, trailing_dot, and inject_field(target_ocsf_path) for log injection.
  - field_isolation_check(source_type, raw, field, op): a WS-2-only invariant (0.04 s per case) asserting that mutating field F changes ONLY F's mapped OCSF path among {group_by paths, distinct_field, class_uid, activity_id, time}. It flags F3 deterministically.
  - Classification of any evasion found, by table lookup and never by tuning: identity-preserving respelling evades means BUG; field-isolation violation means BUG (attribution forgery); silent dead-letter of a well-formed attacker-controlled variant means BUG (silent_drop); non-equivalent respelling means INHERENT (cost reduces to forgone events); not attacker-controlled means NOT_REACHABLE.
5c Axis 2, timing (evasion_axes.py).
  - jitter_scan: amplitude J in {0.5,1,2,5,10,30,50} x the burst's median gap, with K=8 vectors per J from Random(mutate_generic._stable(seed,'jit',J,k)). Report the detected fraction per J and the smallest evading J. An independent exact predictor, window_evades(times, T, W, distinct), reads only timestamps and the YAML, and measured must equal predicted per vector (this catches inclusive/exclusive boundary bugs).
  - optimal_slow_schedule(n, T, W_ms): groups of T-1 events 1 ms apart, next group at W+1 ms after the previous group's first event. It gives the true minimum extra seconds to deliver n events undetected, a cheaper figure than the uniform stretch evasion_search measures. Assert optimal <= uniform and that a schedule 1 ms faster IS detected (the boundary is tight).
  - periodicity rules (common_beaconing): the minimal jitter fraction that lifts the coefficient of variation above max_cv (about sqrt(3)*max_cv for uniform jitter, to be measured rather than trusted).
  - clock_authority probe: for each source_type, report which timestamp wins (F4) and, where the source is attacker-influenced, the stale-stamp evasion. Classify it INHERENT-TO-TRUST-MODEL and always report the owner decision.
  - alert_ids per burst (more than 1 means an epoch-bucket straddle duplicate, the documented Rule.alert_key edge) is informational and never counted as evasion.
5d Axis 3, noise and state exhaustion (noise_dilution.py; the slow WS-8 part uses reg.grade at about 10 s per call).
  (i) State-exhaustion probe, FastProbe only. Inject N benign events that hit the shortest-window rules from disjoint keys, timed so a sweep tick lands while the target rule's key is idle for longer than the short window and shorter than its own window. N is predicted from shared.window._SWEEP_EVERY. Run it for every stateful rule with W greater than the shortest window. It reproduces F1 end to end and measures attacker cost in noise events and seconds.
  (ii) Disjoint-entity flood: sizes 0/50/200/800 noise ALERTS, built as distinct (rule, group, window-bucket) triples using the cheapest rule in the scenario. Measure detection retained, decoy_contamination, campaign coverage, incident_inflation (promoted incidents containing no attack alert), the unchanged attack score (invariant F5) and triage_rank (the position of the first attack alert when alerts are ordered by score then time).
  (iii) Same-entity flood past the WS-8 cap: the predicted N* = member_cap - attack_members_on_track + 1, read from ws8-correlation correlator.DEFAULT_MEMBER_CAP. Measure the retention of attack alert ids in the union of incident member_alert_ids, plus the truncated flag. Since it_intrusion's incident_membership_ok is already False and covered by the campaign view, retention is measured directly on member_alert_ids and not through incident_membership_ok.
  (iv) Event-volume floods are reported as collapsing to at most 2 alert ids (F5).
  Cost is stated in events, alerts and seconds, never in a made-up scalar. The blocking lane runs 2 fixed sizes per scenario. The full bisection and multi-seed runs live behind --full (nightly).
5e Per-rule evasion cost (evasion_cost.py). For every stateful rule-set (a rule plus its companion_of siblings, grouped through siem.companion_of) and a reference burst, compute a VECTOR, never a weighted sum, because converting addresses into seconds would fabricate an exchange rate:
  - forgone_events (loss),
  - extra_seconds (optimal schedule),
  - min_keys[kind] for each key kind the rule-set groups on, with kinds derived from group_by through KEY_KINDS (ip, account, parent_domain, dst target, host, session, ...). An unmapped group_by is reported as unsearchable_key and counted by the coverage gate.
  - joint_frontier: the Pareto-minimal undetected cells of a grid of per-kind key counts, K up to 6 for 2 kinds and up to 4 for 3 kinds, compared with a closed-form prediction (every rule r in the set is evaded iff ceil(n/k_r) < T_r, with a distinct-count variant),
  - respelling_evades and forgery_evades (booleans, expected false),
  - clock_forgeable.
  The reference burst is the storyline burst where one exists. For the 8 uncovered rules, rule_probes.py generates a canonical burst of size 2T from a per-rule template, each template taken from an existing parser test sample and parse-verified. A coverage gate fails when any stateful rule has neither a row nor a dated waiver.
  Reuse evasion_search._first_true, _predict, _combine, _rule_params and the _thin_step/_stretch_step/_spread_step perturbation helpers, extended through a registered kind table. Do not edit the old four-axis predictions, because the existing blocking gate stays as is.
5f Floor and ratchet. evasion_floor.yaml is keyed by rule-set id and records min_keys, joint_frontier_min, max_stealth_rate_per_key, respelling_evades: false, forgery_evades: false, plus a fingerprint of the YAML parameters (threshold, window_seconds, group_by, distinct_field, periodicity, enabled companions). The check fails when a measured value falls below its floor, when a parameter changed without a floor refresh, or when a companion disappears (min_keys for a companion-covered axis falls from 'immune' to a finite number). Floors only ratchet UP automatically; lowering needs --allow-lower --reason, which appends a dated 'lowered:' entry. Rows with ratified: false in evasion_tables.yaml, and floors derived from them, print INFO and do not gate until the owner ratifies them. Initial floors equal the first measured values on the current tree (the measurement is deterministic).
5g Inherent vs bug register (evasion_findings.yaml), the same closed-list pattern as eval/twin/oracle_consistency._ACCEPTED. Each entry has id, class (INHERENT|BUG|TRUST_MODEL), a repro pointer (module and function), status, first_seen and a decision reference. Gate semantics: an unlisted new BUG or INHERENT mismatch FAILS; a listed entry that no longer reproduces FAILS as stale, forcing deletion once fixed; open BUG entries pass but are printed and counted in the artifact (honest status, not a green wash). INHERENT entries (thinning, slowing, spreading across truly distinct entities, non-equivalent respellings) are reported with their predicted-vs-measured agreement and never fixed. Seed entries are F1, F2 and F3 as open BUGs and F4 as TRUST_MODEL.
5h Wiring and determinism. All new modules are stdlib-only (PyYAML is already imported by evasion_search); the output is a pure function of (scenario, seed) with sorted-key JSON, and no set-order dependence, so PYTHONHASHSEED does not matter. Ship in order: 5a with the parity proof, then 5b, 5c, 5e/5f/5g, then 5d, wiring each into run_all_tests.sh as it lands.
positive_and_negative_controls: FastProbe parity, positive: probe_session fired lists equal report._real_detection on the unperturbed it_intrusion stream and on 3 perturbed streams (thin, ip_rotate_2, stretch_6x).
FastProbe parity, negative: a session that deliberately skips the counter reset must FAIL parity. A state-leak test runs A, then B, then A again, and the two A results must be identical.

Sweep repro, positive: the 255-noise-hit scenario against the 300 s distinct rule loses the h1 state today (F1) and the instrument reports an open BUG. Negative: the same noise placed on keys of the SAME window leaves state intact (no finding), and the no-noise run returns count 2. Once the product fix lands the entry goes stale and the gate fails until the entry is deleted.
Field-isolation check, positive: the ssh username-injection variant is flagged because src_endpoint.ip moved. Negative: renaming deploy to deploy2 changes only actor.user.name and is NOT flagged.

Identity classifier, positive: ip2 plus a Windows case/DOMAIN\/trailing-space respelling is classified BUG (identity-preserving). Negative: ip2 plus ssh case-split is classified INHERENT, because the posix_user table says the names are distinct. The DNS case/trailing-dot/deeper-label variants stay detected and are classified robust.

The search must be able to FAIL: with a temp copy of the rules whose group key is replaced by a casefolded one (via FastProbe rules_dir), the previously evading cell becomes detected and the report changes. If the report did not change, the search would be proven rigged.

Timing, positive: J=0 stays detected and J=50x gap evades. Negative: a schedule exactly 1 ms faster than optimal_slow_schedule IS detected, so the boundary is tight. Mutating the predictor by +1 ms must produce a MISMATCH, as the existing (i) control does for the threshold.
Optimal schedule vs uniform stretch: optimal extra_seconds must be less than or equal to the uniform stretch measured by evasion_search._search_stretch for the same burst.

Noise, positive (the metric can go red): a same-entity flood of N* alerts drops attack-alert retention below 1.0 at exactly the predicted N*. Negative: N*-1 keeps retention 1.0, and a disjoint-entity flood of 800 alerts leaves retention at 1.0, decoy_contamination at 0.0 and the attack score unchanged.

Floor, positive: the measured value equals the floor on the current tree and the check is green. Negative A: a temp copy of contracts/rules with common_bruteforce_by_account.yml removed makes ssh_bruteforce's ip_k floor breach (immune becomes 2) and the check fails. Negative B: threshold raised from 10 to 15 in a temp copy lowers the tolerated-loss floor and the check fails with a parameter-fingerprint message. Negative C: a fake stateful rule YAML with no row and no waiver fails the coverage gate.
Ratchet: --update-floor can only raise a value, and lowering without --allow-lower --reason exits non-zero.
Determinism: two same-seed runs give byte-identical JSON, including a subprocess run with PYTHONHASHSEED=0 versus 1.

Applicability honesty: an operator that changes zero events, or that targets a field marked not attacker-controlled, is reported not_searched with its reason and excluded from every rate, mirroring mutate_generic's applicable=False rule.
acceptance: probe_session.verify_parity passes on all 3 storylines, and its negative control (no counter reset) fails; per-probe cost is at most 0.5 s measured, against 3.5-4.7 s today.

evasion_cost.py --seed 7 completes in at most 120 s, covers 100% of the 18 stateful rules (a measured row or a dated waiver; the 8 uncovered rules go through rule_probes.py), and exits 0 on the current tree with the three BUG findings and the one TRUST_MODEL finding recorded as open in evasion_findings.yaml.

The cost artifact reports, per rule-set, the vector (forgone_events, extra_seconds, min_keys per kind, joint_frontier, respelling_evades, forgery_evades, clock_forgeable). No weighted scalar appears anywhere, and every number is tagged basis: harness-measured.

Each of the 4 new axes (obfuscation, timing, noise/state, joint spread) has a documented positive and a negative control in test_evasion_axes.py, and each is wired into run_all_tests.sh. Dropping a companion rule or raising a threshold in a temp rules copy makes the floor check exit non-zero with a message naming the rule, axis, measured value and floor.
Every evasion found is labelled INHERENT, BUG, TRUST_MODEL or NOT_REACHABLE through the tables, with the reason cited. No rule's inherent threshold evasion appears as a 'fix' item.
F1, F2 and F3 are each reproduced by a specific named instrument case, not only by my probes in this design.
The existing evasion_search.py gate output is unchanged (byte-identical JSON on seed 7) unless the parity-gated fast delegation is switched on, and with it on, wall time drops below 60 s.
Same-seed reruns are byte-identical, independent of PYTHONHASHSEED.
A SSOT.md row records each claim as PROVEN or ASSUMED, with the three bugs as OPEN until fixed.
risks: Operator realism: obfuscations a real log source cannot emit would create phantom bugs. This is mitigated by the ATTACKER_CONTROL and IDENTITY_EQUIV tables with a cited basis for every row, and by ratified:false rows being informational only. The tables are security-judgment inputs and need a reviewer.

FastProbe may diverge from the production path through hidden Detector state (rule_last_fired, stats, scorer caches) or ws2 caching. The parity gate, the state-leak test and the negative control are the defence, and the escape hatch FENGARDE_SLOW_PROBE=1 stays.
A closed known-findings list can ossify. Stale detection plus first_seen dates force churn, and open BUG counts are printed in every run.

Floors derived from today's measurement encode today's rule set. The fingerprint check forces a deliberate refresh, but a careless --update-floor could bless a regression, which is why lowering needs an explicit flag and a reason.

The slow WS-8 flood grades cost about 10 s per reg.grade, so a full bisection is minutes per scenario. The blocking lane is limited to fixed sizes and --full is nightly. Large synthetic floods (thousands of events) also grow memory and time in the Correlator.
The F1 repro depends on the exact _SWEEP_EVERY phase (global hit counter), so the instrument must compute the noise count from the counter's own state and not hard-code 255.

Shared files (run_all_tests.sh, ci.yml, SSOT.md, CHANGELOG.md, contracts/detection-coverage.md, eval/adversarial/evasion_search.py) are dirty in the working tree; concurrent edits from other steps risk merge conflicts. Keep my edits to appended blocks.

The product fixes for F1, F2 and F3 are deliberately OUT of scope (this step is measurement). F2 changes alert_key (it embeds the group), so a fix churns alert ids and in-flight dedup across an upgrade.

evasion_search._predict does not understand periodicity and companion metadata. The new module reads them itself and does not patch the old predictor, so two predictors exist until a later consolidation.

The DNS 'upper' probe I ran was invalid, because I upper-cased the 'from' keyword and the parser dropped the line; that case must be written correctly in the real operator (case only inside the QNAME).
needs_owner_decision: Ratify the ATTACKER_CONTROL and IDENTITY_EQUIV tables: which log fields an attacker can really influence per source, and which spellings the source system treats as one entity (Windows case-insensitive, POSIX case-sensitive, DNS case-insensitive). Until ratified, rows are informational and do not gate.

Product bug policy for F2: apply shared.entity_helpers.canonical_entity_value (strip + casefold) to WS-4 group keys, which is consistent with ADR-009 but churns alert_key ids. Stripping DOMAIN\ or the UPN suffix would AMEND the ratified ADR-009 canonical actor definition, and that needs an explicit decision. This step designs only the part that needs neither.

Who fixes F1 (DequeWindowCounter._sweep using the caller's window_ms instead of each key's own window) and F3 (the linux_ssh parser trusting the first ' from <ip>' inside the attacker-supplied username), and on what schedule. This step only measures them and registers them as open BUGs.

WS-8 member_cap eviction policy (currently oldest-first by time): the instrument reports the exact flood size N* that truncates an attack's membership. Whether to change eviction (for example severity-aware) is a product decision. Any change must respect the ratified ADR-009/010 invariant that tracks never merge, so merging tracks to absorb flooding is off the table and not designed here.
Whether triage_rank and incident_inflation under noise are gates or informational. No ratified analyst-queue SLO exists, so I default them to informational.

Timestamp trust policy (F4): whether to add a source-clock-versus-receipt skew guard. Windows, vSphere and CloudTrail ignore receipt time, and a compromised log source can forge it. I report it as TRUST_MODEL and do not design a fix.

Initial floor values and ratchet authority (who may use --allow-lower), and whether a nightly --full lane (multi-seed, WS-8 floods) may be added to .github/workflows/ci.yml, which is already modified in the working tree.

wrong_claims: F5 / noise item (iv) is over-general. alert_key is rule:tenant-group:(time // window), so a flood collapses to <=2 alert ids only when it is one group inside <=2 window buckets. Events spread over many buckets, or over many group keys, give one alert per (group, bucket) that reaches T. Event floods DO create alert floods at a cost of about T events per alert. Item (iv) must report that events-per-alert ratio instead of asserting 'at most 2'.

F5 'Scorer.score is a pure function of the matched rules' is incomplete. services/ws4-detection/scoring.py score() ends in self._apply_exposure(base, event), which depends on the event's asset exposure. The 'attack score unchanged' invariant only holds if exposure is held constant between the flood and no-flood runs.

5e/5f is internally inconsistent. It records respelling_evades:false and forgery_evades:false as floors and says initial floors equal the first measured values on the current tree. On the current tree F2 and F3 are open, so the measured values are true for it_intrusion lateral_movement (which I reproduced) and the ssh rules. Either the floor blesses the bug or the gate cannot exit 0 as acceptance requires. The floor needs a 'waived-by-finding-id' field tied to the evasion_findings.yaml BUG entry, and it must turn into a hard false floor once the finding goes stale.

The F1 repro is not 'N=255 noise events'. DequeWindowCounter._hits counts every hit() or hit_distinct() on any key, and one event hits every stateful rule it matches, including companions. In my end-to-end run (7 lateral_movement events plus ssh noise), as few as 100 noise events removed lateral state and lateral_movement went undetected. Zero or 30 s-late noise stayed detected. A noise count derived from _SWEEP_EVERY must be in counter hits, not events.

The F1 repro also needs the target key idle for longer than the short window at the sweep tick. In my run the burst had to contain a pause of at least 61 s, and a 120 s gap worked. A 62 s gap with noise landing before the next event does not work, because the next event arrives first. The design says this but the cost vector must include the mandatory pause (extra_seconds) as part of F1's cost.

The evasion_search subset shortcut (_detects replays only the step's own events) is invalid for the noise and state axis. The sweep phase depends on the global hit count, which differs between a step-subset replay and a full-stream replay. Parity checks on the baseline plus 3 perturbed streams do not cover noise streams. Noise results are only valid for the exact stream replayed, and parity must be re-proven on noise streams.

Timing claim 'Detector construction costs about 2.4 s of 3.5-4.7 s per probe' does not match my reading. I measured Detector(plugin_rule_dirs=[]) at 1.2-1.4 s and a full slow probe at 1.79 s, while the gate is running. My FastProbe prototype (one Detector, fresh DequeWindowCounter per call, ws2.normalize_one, run_pipeline's ingest_id stamping) took 0.006-0.046 s on dns_exfil (52 events), ssh_bruteforce and lateral_movement, with fired sets identical to run_pipeline. The speed-up is real and larger than claimed, but the baseline numbers were taken under load and should not be cited as fixed.

Appending an 'Evasion cost' table to contracts/detection-coverage.md is not safe as written. tools/check_lane_coverage.py _find_coverage_doc_sources treats any table whose header line starts with '| Rule |' as the rule scorecard and unions every first-column token into the set of covered rules. An evasion table with that header could mask a rule missing from the real scorecard (A3 gate).
missing: Allowlist and suppression axis. Rule evadability also depends on selection predicates and allowlists (contracts/allowlists/*.yml, for example non_geographic_country_codes behind the ZZ sentinel fix, not_in corp_ranges, tenant disabled-rules via load_disabled_rules). The 5f parameter fingerprint (threshold, window, group_by, distinct_field, periodicity, companions) omits the selection and not_in clauses and the allowlist contents, so narrowing a rule's selection or editing an allowlist changes evasion cost without tripping 'parameter changed without floor refresh'.

Floor ratchet direction per metric. 'Floors only ratchet UP' is ambiguous for lower-is-better values such as max_stealth_rate_per_key, extra_seconds and forgone_events. The floor schema needs an explicit better=min|max per field, and a legitimate threshold tune for false positives (rule descriptions invite 'tune per workload') will hard-fail the blocking gate until --allow-lower --reason. Document this as intended friction.

Reachability honesty for the 8 'uncovered' rules. common_impossible_travel fires only on sample RFC 5737 prefixes (its own description says it WILL NOT FIRE on production traffic until a real GeoIP is substituted). Its evasion-cost row measures a sample map, not production, and needs a production_reachable:false tag. Likewise common_bruteforce_sourceless depends on WorkstationName-else-Computer being the group key.

Determinism hazard. Many parsers fall back to int(time.time()*1000) when the timestamp is absent or unparseable (linux_ssh, dns_query, cloudtrail, vmware, windows and others). Obfuscation operators (inject_field, encodings, or any that drop meta.received_at) can hit that path, making output wall-clock dependent and the FastProbe normalisation cache stale. Operators must keep received_at and the verify-by-parse step must flag wall-clock-derived times as not_searched.

Backend parity. F1 is a DequeWindowCounter-only defect (Redis uses per-key EXPIRE). The blocking lane only exercises the deque backend. State that explicitly, and consider a real-Redis half in the style of test_bus_wire_parity (skipped when Redis is absent).

Noise axis ignores the LLM and classifier funnel and the AI queue (AI_QUEUE_CAP, scorer.is_llm_funnel_fresh cooldown), which is the practical analyst or LLM dilution path. Triage_rank and incident_inflation also do not exist yet in eval/twin/report.py. Only decoy_contamination, campaign_decoy_contamination and incident_membership_ok do. They are new metrics to build, not hooks to call.

No cross-reference to existing coverage. mutate.py already has a prompt axis (homoglyph, URL-encode, base64, whitespace; prompt axis 0.4) and mutate_generic already has identity (_split_actor), timing (_jitter 900 ms, _shift) and noise (_decoy) variants. The new operators should reuse or explicitly extend these and state the overlap.

Joint-frontier prediction does not define the assignment function. The closed-form 'ceil(n/k_r) < T_r' for a multi-kind grid needs an explicit mixed-radix round-robin (rank % a, (rank // a) % b). For distinct_field rules (lateral_movement, dns_exfil, port_scan) the per-key count is distinct-values, not events, so the n/k form is only valid when every burst value is distinct.
